reviewedFrom: EP07-01, EP07-02 and EP07-03 (docs/enterprise-production/completion-checklist.json) and the EP07 decisions of 2026-10-14 (a financed buyer's start needs the lender's loan approval with its document on file, a cash buyer proof of funds; throughput targets at division and org scope enforced at release with a reason; per-superintendent limits warn 10 / block 15, past the block an override needs start.release and a reason; a house releases only with a superintendent, assigned in one atomic transaction; crew calendars deferred). Code: lib/services/starts.ts (deriveAutoGate agreement_milestones_clear, assertReleaseGateCompletion, releaseStart, setProjectSuperintendent, listSuperintendentCandidates); lib/services/even-flow.ts (setThroughputTarget, getThroughputWeeks, setReleaseSlot); lib/services/superintendent-capacity.ts; lib/starts/{gate-logic,close-impact,superintendent-load}.ts; migration 20261014100000_starts_capacity_and_throughput (proof-of-funds milestone, release_throughput_targets, superintendent_capacity, assign_project_superintendent, queue_start_release replaced, community_release_slots and projects.superintendent_id locked to the server). Fixture: one production builder from production-seed whose first tranche (lots 1-10) is developed; a viewer and a project lead (project.manage, start.write, no start.release or start.slots).

starts-financing-gate-holds-financed-sal.derivation: A financed sale on lot 1: the package opens with the financing gate pending (nothing attached is absence, not a pass). The loan application satisfied (no document needed) still holds it. The loan approval satisfied with a file on the home clears it. Reopening the approval holds it again; a waiver holds it (a waiver is not a document). Satisfied again with a second file, the gate clears; archiving that file holds it again. A cash sale on lot 2 seeds one start-holding proof-of-funds milestone that needs evidence; the gate is pending until it is satisfied with a file, then passes.

starts-attested-evidence-archived-before.derivation: The org defines a manual gate, Soil report on file. A spec home on lot 4 has it attested with the report as a file on the home, and the package is ready; the spec home's financing gate passed because a spec has no buyer. The report is archived before the release runs. Publication re-checks the attested file, so the home does not release (it stays held in releasing for retry) and the job's error names the soil_report gate's evidence.

starts-release-without-superintendent-is.derivation: A ready spec home on lot 5 with no superintendent: releaseStart refuses (service) and queue_start_release refuses (database); the package stays ready. With the superintendent assigned and then suspended from the org, the database refuses again (not an active member). Reinstated, the release queues.

starts-assigning-past-capacity-is-refuse.derivation: Relative to the houses the superintendent already runs (base): the org default is stretched at base+1 and limited at base+2. Two houses are assigned; the third answers requiresOverride (the coordinator can override, 2 houses against a limit of 2 over base) and stays unassigned. A project lead with a reason is refused (the override needs start.release), and a reason shorter than ten characters is refused. The picker reports the person 2 houses in, warned at 1, limit 2, none remaining, load over. The person's own limits (base+3 warn, base+4 limit) outrank the default, so the third house now assigns. With their limit at base+3 a fourth is refused at the limit, then a releaser assigns it with the reason; the audit records over_capacity and the reason and the house is scoped to them. A project lead cannot set limits. The org is left on the built-in ten and fifteen.

race-two-assignments-to-the-last-open-ca.derivation: The person runs one more house than before against a limit of two more. Two independent database sessions, released together, each assign a different house to them: the serial-equivalent outcome is exactly one assigned and one told the limit, and the person ends two houses over their starting count (the held one and the winner). Two rounds.

starts-division-throughput-cap-spans-com.derivation: Bayshore, a second community of the Gulf Coast division, already released one house this week (fixture). The division's target for the week is 1: a viewer cannot set it, the coordinator can. Releasing a Cypress Landing house answers that the division is over (target 1, 1 already) and changes nothing; a reason under ten characters is refused; with a real reason it releases, and the audit and the start.released_over_slot event carry it. With the division target lifted and an org-wide target of 2, the next house is held by the org cap (target 2, 2 already: Bayshore's and the first). The desk reads the org cap as 2 of 2.

race-two-releases-into-one-throughput-ca.derivation: Two ready houses target the same future week under a division cap of one. Two independent sessions call queue_start_release together: exactly one is queued, the other is held by the division cap, and one package is releasing. Two rounds, on different weeks.

starts-division-scoped-coordinator-canno.derivation: A starts coordinator limited to the Treasure Coast division, with a planning house in Gulf Coast and one in Treasure Coast. Assigning the Gulf Coast house is refused by the service (the house is not in their division), and the assignment function refuses it on its own when called with their id. The house stays unassigned. Assigning the Treasure Coast house works. Setting the org default superintendent limits and the org-wide throughput target are refused (they need reach over the whole organization). With the person also holding the Gulf Coast house, the picker the coordinator sees counts the same houses the assignment does.

starts-viewer-cannot-write-slots-or-targ.derivation: The coordinator sets a community slot through the service and it is audited once. A viewer's setReleaseSlot is refused, and so are their direct REST writes: updating or inserting a community slot, inserting a throughput target or a superintendent limit, and assigning a superintendent on a project. A project lead (no start.slots, no start.release) cannot set a target or a limit. The slot stays at 3 and the house stays unassigned.

starts-release-impact-preview-matches-cl.derivation: A sold home on lot 3 with its closing scheduled 100 days out and the default 130-day cycle (no community cycle configured): the must-start date is 30 days ago. Starting today projects a close on day 130, 30 days late; starting 30 days out, 60 days late; had it started 30 days ago, it closes on day 100 with no slack. A week four weeks out is a later start than today. One home is pushed past its closing by the 30-day start.
